clue.text: Young offender wearing headgear? That's clear

indicators.note: the headgear has the young offender on, so the one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A young delinquent in a cap: the situation seems plain enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young offender' suggests a criminal, but here it is just a cheeky child.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: limpid water or prose is transparent and easily understood.

clue.text: Relaxed call in effect?

parts.note: to dial is to call; laid is dial spelt backwards, so ... says dial, a call

explanation.surface: A chilled call, in effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: LAID put back gives DIAL, which means call.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone easygoing and unhurried is described as laid-back.

clue.text: Prank interrupting senior minister is nonsense

indicators.note: the prank breaks into the minister's name

parts.note: Theresa May was then Home Secretary, a senior cabinet minister
a lark is a bit of fun or a prank

explanation.surface: A practical joke disrupting a senior politician is silly behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: May was Home Secretary when this was set, before becoming Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: malarkey is informal for foolish talk or humbug.

clue.text: Work of thin European expert gets exposed

indicators.note: the word thin is worked into a new order

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: A skinny European specialist's work is unmasked.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being naked, with nothing covering the body, is being in the buff.

clue.text: Kim's hair's straggling without a brush

indicators.note: hair that straggles is untidy and out of place, so the letters are rearranged
tells us the letter a is to be taken out of the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Kim has no hairbrush, so the hair is a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from KIMSHAIRS and rearrange the rest. 'Brush' looks like a hairbrush but is a minor clash.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brush with the enemy is a brief fight, a minor engagement.

clue.text: Lacking degree initially, risk doom telling unstable student of politics abroad

indicators.note: letters that are unstable are shaken into a new order
tells us one letter is missing from the pool
takes the opening letter of degree

explanation.surface: Without a qualification, warning of disaster makes a politics student shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop D from RISKDOOMTELLING and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Kremlinologist studied Soviet government, a foreign political system.

clue.text: Cousins, maybe, died with one in service

indicators.note: the death and the one go inside the service

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
ob. is short for obiit, Latin for died
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Relatives perhaps died, one of them while serving in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cousins' is not relatives but Robin Cousins, the British Olympic figure skating champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Robin Cousins won Olympic skating gold for Britain in 1980.

clue.text: Popular second quiz presenter not having arrived for the moment

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the presenter's name is shown without the arrival letters

parts.note: Chris Tarrant hosted Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: A well-liked quiz host is absent for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: TARRANT without ARR gives TANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an instant is a very brief point in time.

clue.text: Loathing out-of-order description of Cooper's trademark?

indicators.note: the two parts swap places, so the end comes round to the front

parts.note: the comedian Tommy Cooper always wore a red fez, a red hat

explanation.surface: Disgust at a garbled account of a comic's signature look.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a British comedian famous for his red fez.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hatred is intense dislike or loathing.

clue.text: Cook has ended snack following cold ham to demonstrate this?

definitions.text: Cook has ended snack following cold ham to demonstrate this?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the cold letter
to cook is to fiddle or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy cook who has messed up a snack after the cold ham shows clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' hints at ham-fisted; the scene itself illustrates the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being clumsy or awkward with the hands, like a fumbling cook.

clue.text: Breather with no end of panting by a guy that's embarrassed

indicators.note: signals that a letter is dropped from the breather

parts.note: a gill is how a fish breathes

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word panting

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: Someone out of breath standing by a man who is red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest, but it is a fish's organ; GILL loses G, the last letter of 'panting'. 'Guy' is a verb, to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being uncomfortable and self-conscious in company is the same as feeling embarrassed.

clue.text: Swarm around — get prepared?

definitions.meaning: to crowd in on all sides, as bees or troubles do
read as two words, to be made ready, as in 'ready, steady'

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be besieged is to be swarmed around; split, the letters say become ready.

clue.text: Mad addict losing head in grip of fool

indicators.note: the fool holds the shortened addict inside

parts.note: berk is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: the first letter of the addict is dropped

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: A crazed junkie being restrained by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' drops the addict's first letter and 'in grip of' puts the rest inside the fool; 'berk' is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: going berserk means acting in a wild, frenzied way, like a madman.

clue.text: Evidence of a poet with mellow pedigree

parts.note: a line of verse is what a poet produces
to age is to mellow with time, as wine or cheese does

explanation.surface: A sign of a poet who has an aged, mellow ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pedigree is the ancestry or line of descent of a person or animal.

clue.text: Ape with tail moving for all to see — and aquatic rodent

indicators.note: the last letter of the imitation word shifts to a new place

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A monkey swinging its tail alongside a water-dwelling rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' is a verb, to copy; the tail Y moves back one place to give COYP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the coypu, or nutria, is a large South American rodent living in rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Offer comment with a Northern collection of art closed?

parts.note: if the Tate gallery collection were shut, there would be no Tate

explanation.surface: A northerner remarking that the art gallery is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the famous London art gallery; when closed, the visitor finds 'no Tate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to annotate a text is to add explanatory remarks or notes to it.

clue.text: Casual line retained by actor before a play's finale

indicators.note: the line is held inside the actor's name

parts.note: John Thaw was a British actor, known as Inspector Morse
a row is a line

indicators.note: takes the last letter of play's

explanation.surface: An offhand line held back by an actor until the play's end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a throwaway remark is casual, made without emphasis.

clue.text: Violent behaviour hurt eg discontented guy needing treatment

indicators.note: the letters need treating, so they are worked into a new order
the contents are removed, leaving the outer letters of guy

explanation.surface: A disgruntled man who was hurt needs medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thuggery is brutish violent conduct, as by thugs.

clue.text: In Irish house, return to remove flower

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the Irish house

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: the word for remove is read backwards

parts.note: to doff is to take off, as a hat

explanation.surface: Instructions to go back into an Irish house and take away a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return to remove' reads like going back to fetch something, but 'return' reverses the word for remove; the Dáil is Ireland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the daffodil is a yellow spring bloom, also the national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: A rule reportedly put into legal question

indicators.note: means the words are as spoken

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A regulation is said to have been brought into legal dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Auntie's inspiration's floral tribute to be picked up

indicators.note: picked up as in heard on the radio, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a wreath is a ring of flowers laid at a funeral

explanation.surface: An aunt's inspiration was a funeral wreath someone had to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' is a British nickname for the BBC; Lord Reith was its founding director-general.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: John Reith shaped the BBC's public service ideals, its guiding inspiration.

clue.text: Upstanding look in untrained figure abandoning church, one from Africa?

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from bottom to top
the look goes inside the novice minus church
the church letters leave the untrained figure

parts.note: a novice is a beginner
CE is the Church of England
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: An upright look on a beginner who has left the church, perhaps an African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' leaves NOVI; 'in' places the look after its N, and 'Upstanding' turns the whole NAIROVI upwards. The question mark flags that Africa holds many nationalities.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivory Coast, is an Ivorian.

clue.text: Twig in measure of water

definitions.meaning: to twig is British slang for to understand, grasp
a unit of six feet for sea depth

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to grasp something is to understand it; also a nautical depth unit of six feet.

clue.text: Fool, one that might be apparent, we hear, with cape

indicators.note: says the word is as spoken rather than written

parts.note: an heir apparent is next in line to inherit
a head is a headland, a cape

explanation.surface: A fool, apparently, and wearing a cape too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparent' points to 'heir apparent'; HEIR spoken sounds like AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an airhead is a silly, empty-headed person.

clue.text: Praise one that's left union over French department getting promotion

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in a down entry, promoting the word moves it upward, reading backwards

parts.note: the Lot is a département in southwest France

explanation.surface: A former partner moves up in the French civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Cricketer dropping first of edges, supported by leader in gully and slip

indicators.note: the cricketer loses a letter

parts.note: David Gower was an England batsman

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of edges

parts.note: on means resting upon, supported by

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of gully

explanation.surface: A cricketer dropping a catch off the edge in the gully and slip fielding positions.
explanation.walkthrough: Gully and slip are close catching positions in cricket; 'edges' are snicks off the bat. GOWER loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to slip up is to make a mistake or err.

clue.text: Raise army around island

indicators.note: the army surrounds the island letter

parts.note: a host is a large army

explanation.surface: Troops are lifted up around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hoist is to lift up, as a flag or a sail.

clue.text: Former holiday period with time travelling west, captured in edited reels

indicators.note: the holiday piece sits inside the rearranged reels
film reels that are edited are cut and rearranged
west is leftward in an across entry, so the time letter moves to the front

parts.note: Whit is Whitsun, the Pentecost holiday

explanation.surface: A holiday film shot over time, now cut from edited reels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling west' moves the time letter to the front of Whit, the Whitsun holiday; 'edited' gives ERSLE and 'captured in' holds the holiday inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: erstwhile means previous or one-time, as in an erstwhile friend.

clue.text: One indulging in beef, reportedly, and lamb initially is a picture

indicators.note: points to the word as heard in non-rhotic speech

parts.note: to beef is to complain, so a complainer is a moaner

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A meat-eater enjoying beef and lamb: a picture of contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is slang for a grumble, not meat; MOANER said in British speech sounds like MONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Leonardo's Mona Lisa is the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Recitation of poet once in coastal city

indicators.note: a recitation is spoken, so the word is as heard

parts.note: Sir Philip Sidney was an Elizabethan poet

explanation.surface: Reciting the work of an old poet in a seaside city.
